```sql
-- name: top_customers
-- owner: sales
-- params: tenant_id, from, to, limit
-- Customers ranked by revenue, with their most recent order. Only customers
-- whose last order falls inside the window are listed; this is what the
-- account managers asked for ("who was active this quarter").
WITH order_agg AS (
    SELECT o.customer_id,
           sum(o.total_cents) AS revenue,
           count(*)           AS order_count,
           max(o.created_at)  AS last_order_at
      FROM orders o
     WHERE o.status IN ('paid', 'processing', 'shipped', 'delivered')
     GROUP BY o.customer_id
)
SELECT c.id,
       c.email,
       c.company,
       c.country_code,
       a.revenue,
       a.order_count,
       a.last_order_at
  FROM customers c
  JOIN order_agg a ON a.customer_id = c.id
 WHERE c.tenant_id = %(tenant_id)s
   AND a.last_order_at >= %(from)s
   AND a.last_order_at <  %(to)s
 ORDER BY a.revenue DESC
 LIMIT %(limit)s
```

De originele query koppelde de geaggregeerde CTE's via een nested loop die de hele totalen-aggregatie per rij herhaalde (ruim 48 miljoen verworpen join-rijen). Door de orders in één keer per klant te groeperen met `max(created_at)` als laatste bestelling, en pas daarna met `customers` te joinen, verdwijnt die kwadratische lus. Het resultaat blijft gelijk, al is de volgorde van gelijke omzetwaarden bij `LIMIT` ook in het origineel niet gegarandeerd.
